free_tier.stated: paid $1.35/TB/month stored + $1.00/TB egress (cut from $1.50/$2.00 on 1 Sep 2026, an 18% total reduction). Paid in USDC on Ethereum, not STORJ.
free_tier.notes: a payout for storing and serving other users' data on a node the user runs, not a free allowance

egress.terms: you are paid $1.00/TB for egress; the customer is charged $7/TB

interface_detail: Docker container, single identity per node, dashboard
tooling: storagenode Docker image, storj node dashboard, uptime robot
chaining: USDC payout can be spent on anything, but cannot be converted into Storj storage credit - there is no credit mechanism
limits_note: Worse ratio than Sia and stated in the same currency, which makes it unambiguous: SNO gets $1.35/TB while Storj charges the customer $7.00/TB for the same terabyte - a 5.2x gap. To fund 20 TiB at $7/TB ($140/mo) plus 30 TiB/mo egress at $7/TB ($210/mo) = $350/mo, you must store $350/1.35 = 259 TB of other people's data. Storj's own forum arithmetic also carries a 2.7x erasure expansion factor, so 1 TB of customer data consumes 2.7 TB of SNO disk - meaning the true disk ratio is ~700 TB contributed to consume 20 TB. This is the clearest negative in the slot.

identity_cost.detail: the node is configured with an email address and an Ethereum wallet address for USDC payouts; no authorization token is needed to join

reliability_note: Node disqualification and held amounts apply for the first months; forum reports of 8.5 TiB stored paying $5.50 indicate realised rates well below list.

evidence.proved: Standard: 'Monthly storage $7/TB', 'Egress $7/TB'; minimum monthly fee $5; 30-day minimum retention with early-deletion fee; 50 KB minimum object size
rate table: 'Used space (storage) $1.50/TB/month -> $1.35/TB/month -10%'; 'Egress (bandwidth) $2.00/TB -> $1.00/TB -50%'; 'estimated 18% reduction in total payout'
'Payouts are made in USD Coin (USDC) ... Earnings are calculated in USD and paid at one USDC per US dollar'
'$1.5/TB is for a single SNO, but theres 2.7 expansion factor, so 1 TB times 2.7 times $1.5 = $4.05 just a storage cost, per month'
'for 2026/09 my node stored 8.5 TiB of data and was paid $5.50'
the node's run command takes a wallet address and an email address
evidence.quote: 1. Edit the `WALLET`, `EMAIL`, `ADDRESS`, `STORAGE` and replace the `<identity-dir>`, and `<storage-dir>` with your parameters.

evidence.proved: node operators are paid for the storage and bandwidth their nodes provide
evidence.quote: Storj nodes share underutilized hard drive capacity and bandwidth with the Storj network and are paid when users store and retrieve data.

evidence.proved: the authorization-token step for a new node identity is no longer required
a payout is withheld until its transaction fee is at most 25% of its value
evidence.quote: We will not send a transaction where the fee for the transaction is more than 25% of the value of the transaction.

evidence.proved: the September 1 change cut storage pay from $1.50 to $1.35 per TB-month and egress pay from $2.00 to $1.00 per TB, an estimated 18% total cut
evidence.quote: Combined, this represents an estimated 18% reduction in total payout

evidence.proved: node operators are paid $1.35 per TB-month stored and $1.00 per TB of egress, in USDC on Ethereum

notes: Payout rates since Sep 1st, 2026: USD 1.35 per TB-month stored, USD 1.00 per TB of egress and USD 1.00 per TB of audit and repair traffic, paid in USDC on Ethereum layer 1; zkSync layer 2 payouts ended on September 1, 2026, and a payout is sent only when its transaction fee is at most 25% of its value, so smaller balances roll into later months.

dead_end.why: paid $1.35/TB/month stored + $1.00/TB egress (cut from $1.50/$2.00 on 1 Sep 2026, an 18% total reduction). Paid in USDC on Ethereum, not STORJ.
